gloss: to leave, to go away, to depart

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{町|まち}を{去|さ}った。

examples.english: Don't chase after those who leave.

examples.japanese: {職場|しょくば}を{去|さ}ることにした。
examples.english: I decided to leave the workplace.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}が{去|さ}り、{春|はる}が{来|き}た。
{長年|ながねん}{働|はたら}いた{会社|かいしゃ}を{去|さ}るのは{寂|さび}しかった。
examples.english: It was sad to leave the company where I had worked for many years.

examples.japanese: {痛|いた}みが{去|さ}ったあと、ようやく{眠|ねむ}ることができた。
examples.english: After the pain passed, I was finally able to sleep.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}が{舞台|ぶたい}を{去|さ}ったあとも、{拍手|はくしゅ}はしばらく{続|つづ}いていた。
examples.english: Even after he left the stage, the applause continued for a while.

notes:
{去|さ}る is a literary verb meaning to leave or depart, more formal than {離|はな}れる or {出|で}る.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive)
- Takes を particle to mark the place being left

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {場所|ばしょ}を{去|さ}る: to leave a place
- {故郷|こきょう}を{去|さ}る: to leave one's hometown
- {時|とき}が{去|さ}る: time passes
- {嵐|あらし}が{去|さ}る: the storm passes

PROVERBS:
- {去|さ}る{者|もの}は{追|お}わず: Don't chase those who leave
- {去|さ}る{者|もの}{日日|ひび}に{疎|うと}し: Out of sight, out of mind

IN COMPOUNDS:
{去|きょ} reading in compounds: {去年|きょねん} (last year), {過去|かこ} (the past)

DON'T CONFUSE:
{猿|さる} (monkey) has the same reading.
